The claim excludes the even-parity zero-scale branches, where the simple-root argument in z is not applicable.

value.rationale: The published result gives only a universal coefficient \(5.51\), while the exact factorization exposes the actual high-energy cluster geometry and its dependence on parity and fivefold symmetry. The improvement is structural rather than a cosmetic numerical tightening: it identifies the finite energy offsets of the nonzero branches, reveals golden-ratio constants in odd cells, and separates sectors that the published enclosure merges. These constants are natural inputs for perturbative splitting, degeneracy, and comparison questions on finite quantum graphs.
